headline: Authorities Say 244 Foreigners Were Apprehended in Zamboanga Sibugay Raids on Suspected POGO Hubs
seoTitle: 244 Foreigners Apprehended in Zamboanga Sibugay POGO Raids
seoDescription: The Bureau of Immigration says 244 foreign nationals were apprehended at two suspected POGO sites in Zamboanga Sibugay. The NBI director put the count at 234.
deck: The Bureau of Immigration says those apprehended are under investigation for alleged immigration and POGO-related violations. No one has been charged or convicted in the reports reviewed for this article.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: Immigration, National Bureau of Investigation and Armed Forces of the Philippines personnel raided two suspected offshore gaming sites in Zamboanga Sibugay on Friday, October 2, the Bureau of Immigration said in a statement released Sunday, October 4. The sites are in Barangay Kimos, Siay, and Barangay Tandiong Muslim, Alicia.

The BI said 113 foreign nationals were apprehended in Siay and 131 in Alicia, for 244 in total, most of them Chinese. It described the operation as the largest POGO bust of 2026. Separately, NBI Director Melvin Matibag told DZRH on Monday, October 5, that the NBI count was 234 arrests and that investigators were examining nearly 4,000 devices. The two agency totals have not been reconciled in the public statements reviewed for this report.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The BI said those apprehended are being investigated for alleged immigration violations, including working without the proper visa, being undocumented and illegal entry, and for alleged involvement in illegal POGO-related online activity. Identities and nationalities remain subject to verification, the bureau said.

Authorities reported recovering 78 computer monitors and about 3,000 mobile phones, laptops and SIM cards from the Siay compound, which the BI said pointed to an organised online operation. Matibag said the NBI is examining how long the sites had operated, whether government officials were involved, and possible troll-farm activity. He also said people were rescued who were allegedly victims of forced labor, trafficking and physical abuse. Those claims are investigation leads, not court findings.
Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators have been banned under Executive Order 74 (2024). Reports also cite Republic Act 12312, the Anti-POGO Act of 2025, as part of the legal basis for the crackdown.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Scam hubs of this kind are tied in official statements to love scams and trafficking, which can affect Filipino victims and workers. Those apprehended face deportation proceedings according to the BI, and anyone with a deportation order would be blacklisted. They have not been convicted of any offence, and the allegations have not been tested in court.

FMB News did not find a Chinese government statement on the raids in the sources checked for this article. Philstar reported that the Chinese embassy had not responded when asked by Agence France-Presse.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a reconciled headcount from the BI and NBI, charging or deportation decisions, any findings on alleged official involvement, and further operations against similar suspected sites elsewhere in Mindanao and the Visayas.

audit.verificationNotes: BI 244 total (113 Siay / 131 Alicia) is consistent across Philstar, Rappler, Inquirer and ABS-CBN. NBI Director Matibag's 234 figure and device count come from DZRH on 5 Oct. Count conflict is attributed, not resolved. Trafficking and official-involvement language is framed as NBI investigation leads. No person or pension-house business name is used. No Chinese government reply found when rechecked on the afternoon of 5 Oct.
